doc: The one write rule (pacific_wire::address). A tag is an Ed25519 verifying key and a pub
carries a signature by it; a relay that checks refuses anything else. The key comes from a
32-byte seed the writer already holds. Both repos test against the vector below: the relay
through pacific-wire itself, the Python harness through its second implementation.
address.kdf: HKDF-SHA256(salt = key_label, ikm = seed, info = "v1") -> the Ed25519 signing key; the tag is its verifying key
address.signed: sig_domain || tag (32 bytes) || blob as sent (the base64 string's bytes)

why: This file is the Semaphore wire spec that arc/docs/arc-api-icd-v1.html §6 points at.
It exists because the relay's tests used to assert its Frame enum AGAINST ITSELF, and the
client's tests asserted its own enum against itself, so the two drifted into three
incompatible generations at once (5 variants at arc HEAD, 6 in pacific-wire, 10 on the live
box). The drift was fatal, not cosmetic: an unknown variant fails Frame::from_json, which
pacific-core/src/transport.rs maps to CoreError::Transport, which kills the sync drain.
There is now ONE enum (pacific_wire::Frame, which the relay re-exports) and this fixture is
the third party both sides are held to: pacific-wire asserts the client enum against it and
arc/planes/relay asserts the server against it. A Frame variant cannot be added, renamed or
re-encoded in either repo without this file changing too.

note: A client declares the frames it can PARSE in Sub.v, and the relay may send it nothing
above that. This is not politeness: an unknown relay->client frame is FATAL on the client,
so a relay that has learned a new frame may never simply start sending it.
Sub.v is absent on the wire when 0, so a client that predates a level is byte-identical to
what it always sent and is never handed a frame it cannot read.
min_v below is the floor for BOTH directions: the relay will not send a frame above the
connection's declared v, and will not act on an inbound request above it either (it drops
the request in silence, because every answer it could give is itself above the floor).

levels.meaning: the mailbox. Every build ever shipped.
retention is announced: the replayed backlog may be incomplete.
presigned object-storage offload. No shipping client declares this yet.

frames.doc: Store this blob under tag and fan it out. The tag is an Ed25519 verifying key and sig is its signature over "pacific-relay-pub:v1\n" || tag bytes || blob-as-sent (pacific_wire::address); a relay that checks refuses anything else. commit:true claims the tag's single commit slot.
Subscribe to tags; replay seq > since, then Eose, then live. v declares the client's vocabulary.
A stored or live blob on tag, with its monotonic seq.

The verdict on a Pub. ok:false means nothing was stored. reason names why (malformed_tag, not_a_key, malformed_sig, bad_signature, too_large, rate_limited, busy, full); it is absent only when a commit lost its tag's slot, which is an instruction to rebase rather than an error.
The backlog just replayed for tag is INCOMPLETE: blobs at or below floor were evicted.
End of the stored backlog for the current Sub; live follows. Exactly one per Sub.
Presign an upload of key, bounded to exactly len bytes (len is signed into the URL).
Presign a download of key. The relay does not check existence — a blind relay cannot.
A short-lived presigned URL for key, valid only for the method it was signed for.
The presign was refused. reason is a stable token: unconfigured | bad_key | too_large | over_budget | budget_stale.
